action_items.text: Review the minutes from the last meeting posted on Project Share.
Investigate whether it is possible to implement a text-only TV guide preview on the remote control instead of an LCD screen.
Research if there is a standard menu button usable across different TV brands to allow a universal remote to access complicated functions.
Look into whether the changeable covers should include the buttons themselves or just be a sleeve over them.
Conduct trend-watching to understand what people really want regarding the components and design of the remote control.
Put ideas for different remote control shapes and colors on paper to present at the next meeting.
Find out if rechargeable batteries are possible and if people are willing to pay extra for them.
Find out what people are willing to pay for the remote control.
Research the cost and space requirements for an LCD screen.
Research the cost and space requirements for speech recognition.
Think of a name for the product.

decisions.text: The target demographic for the new remote control is people under forty years old.
The Teletext button should be kept but not made a primary button; it should be placed under a secondary menu or option.
The remote control should feature changeable covers to appeal to different tastes and allow for language-specific covers for older people, rather than manufacturing entirely new remote bodies.
The LCD screen for channel preview should be removed due to high cost and battery consumption.
Speech recognition should not be implemented in the remote control yet because the technology is not mature, requires too much memory, and is not ready for a global market.
The remote control should be a universal remote control rather than a brand-specific one.
The remote control design should be distinct from competitors (like Sony) to avoid confusion, potentially using different shapes or curves.
The power button should be on top.
The mute button should be placed around the volume selection, not at the top.
The channel buttons should be on top.
The channel up and down buttons should be grouped together.
The channel button should be in the center.
If an LCD screen is possible and not too expensive, it should be included.
